question.problem: Find the inverse of the function $f(x)=-\frac{2}{3}\sqrt[3]{x}.$
question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
y=-\frac{2}{3}\sqrt[3]{x}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
x=-\frac{2}{3}\sqrt[3]{y}.
$$

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-\frac{2}{3}\sqrt[3]{y} \\ \sqrt[3]{y} & =-\frac{3}{2}x \\ (\sqrt[3]{y})^{3} & ={(-\frac{3}{2}x)}^{3} \\ y & =-\frac{27}{8}{x}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=-\frac{27}{8}{x}^{3}.
$$
